newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Bozano dismisses reports on audit of Banerj.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Bozano dismisses reports on audit of Banerj.

text.p: The manager of state bank Banerj dismissed press reports that the Rio de Janeiro state Accounting Office (TCE) has ordered an in depth audit of the bank.

Newspapers today said the TCE was accusing Bozano, Simonsen, the bank assigned to manage Banerj and ready it for privatization, of withholding information on Banerj's financial performance, which forms the basis for its remuneration for administering the state bank.
Bozano said it has not received any notification from the TCE, adding the TCE has had five auditors working full time to oversee Banerj's management since January 15.
"We have not received any notification from the TCE (to conduct an in depth audit) and, if it does so, there is no problem. We have nothing to hide," said Paulo Ferraz, Bozano's president.
Ferraz said Bozano has never refused to provide information on Banerj to TCE's auditors.
"Everything that they asked was answered," he said.

Ferraz lashed out at the reports, which also said the TCE wanted Bozano to return seven million reais of the 43 million reais it has received because the management contract limits its remuneration to 36 million reais.
"The seven million reais have already been returned," he said, adding the procedure followed changes approved in the contract.
Early this year, Bozano was awarded a contract by Rio de Janeiro state government to manage Banerj, replacing the Central Bank, and prepare it for a sell-off in 1997.
